explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is someone who works aboard ship, the ordinary word for a sailor.

clue.text: Quarrel a lot? Rubbish!

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a big row with a scornful exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' reads as an exclamation of disbelief, but it is the definition as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrapheap is where discarded junk ends up, so the word stands for rubbish or things thrown away.

explanation.walkthrough: The '&and' is how the scan was read; the printed clue joins the sailor and the answer with 'and'. AB stands for able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is formal release from guilt or blame, close in sense to being cleared or vindicated.

clue.text: One may produce notes on the French bean

second meaning: a small pale-green kidney bean

explanation.surface: Someone jots notes about a particular bean variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests writing, but here they are musical notes from a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small fipple flute that plays tunes and a kind of haricot bean grown in France.

clue.text: Cars negotiating bends

blocks.note: the letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Arcs are curved lines or sections of a circle, which is what bends are.

clue.text: 29 gloomy — in a state? No, quite the opposite

blocks.note: drear is a poetic word for dismal or gloomy
ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a gloomy person is in a state, and is told the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue first says gloomy goes in a state, then reverses it: the state goes inside gloomy, after its fourth letter. 29 is IDEALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist and a dreamer are both people who pursue impractical visions rather than reality.

clue.text: Note in winning it's all relative

explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' looks like victory, but it means charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of a sibling, so she is a relative.

clue.text: The enchanting creature is through with one

blocks.note: per means by way of or through, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A magical creature has finished with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is through with' reads as having finished with; 'through' alone gives the preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian legend a peri is a beautiful fairy or spirit, a creature of enchantment.

clue.text: Put out, not for the first time, about a matter of contention

definitions.text: Put out, not for the first time

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
an issue is a disputed point

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed again over a disputed point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests annoyed, but it means published.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue is to publish or release something again after an earlier edition.

clue.text: Attract a number to a Mediterranean island

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Drawing a crowd of people to a Greek holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to gather or grow by drawing material onto itself, so it attracts additions.

clue.text: Broadcast in favour of new medical treatment

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters are formed into a fresh arrangement
giving letters a treatment works them over into a different order

blocks.note: pro means for or supporting
the letters of this word, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like a noun for a programme, but it is a past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To have proclaimed something is to have announced it publicly, spreading it widely as broadcasting does.

clue.text: One among the pirates meeting in Penzance? No

indicators.note: something among other words is sitting inside them, spanning their join

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and the start of the second
surface padding: a wry aside that this pirate belongs to another story

explanation.surface: Asking whether a character belongs to the pirates of Gilbert and Sullivan's Penzance, and answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Captain Hook's bosun in Peter Pan: a pirate, but not one of The Pirates of Penzance, hence 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is one of the pirates in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan, Hook's loyal right-hand man.

clue.text: Turning pale, proved to have had too much to drink

definitions.text: to have had too much to drink
definitions.note: a cryptic reading: lapped (drunk) to excess

indicators.note: turning things over changes their order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone going white shows they have been drinking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as over + lapped: to lap is to drink like a cat, so overdoing it is to have over-lapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Split playfully, the word means having lapped up liquor beyond the limit, a whimsical sense rather than its usual one of covering partly.

clue.text: He'll raise a point with a man of the cloth

blocks.note: E for east, a point of the compass
a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman will bring up a point in discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise a point' suggests debate; the definition is just 'He'll raise', someone who builds or sets things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is one who puts up or raises structures, a person who erects.

clue.text: Rogues who engage in smuggling valuable stones

blocks.note: to run guns or drugs is to smuggle them
agates are banded semi-precious stones

explanation.surface: Villains who smuggle precious gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Runagate is an archaic word for a vagabond, fugitive or renegade, hence a rogue.

clue.text: The little beast's allowed outside at all times

blocks.note: let means allowed, as in let go
ever means always

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' suggests outdoors; here it tells one word to go around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare in its first year, so a little beast.

clue.text: A bird that changes its modulation?

explanation.surface: A bird that varies the pitch of its song.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's name split in two reads as turns tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a wading bird that flips over stones on the shore to find food.

clue.text: A unit inordinately wrapped up in design

too means excessively

explanation.walkthrough: The extra word goes inside the design word just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a military unit, a subdivision of a company commanded by a lieutenant.

clue.text: Mean to get a beverage and be blowed!

clue.text: One struggling to hold Her Majesty's dog

ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher.

clue.text: Ready and willing to make complaint

clue.text: Though drab, the colour is uniform

clue.text: The chef's whiskers!

clue.text: Broken sculpture
